scope: Standard Transformer KV payload derivation, GQA example, V1 cache planning, quantized KV cache, metrics and offloading.

claims.claim: For a standard full-attention Transformer with uniform layers, theoretical K/V payload is approximately 2 × layers × KV heads × head dimension × tokens × bytes per element.
claims.locator: Cache dtype configuration; formula derived from K and V tensor shapes
claims.notes: Excludes scale metadata, alignment, special layouts and runtime overhead.

claims.claim: Multi-Query Attention (Shazeer, 2019) and Grouped-Query Attention (Ainslie et al., 2023) reduce the number of key/value heads, which directly shrinks saved K/V state per token.
claims.locator: GQA abstract and method; MQA from arXiv:1911.02150
claims.notes: The chapter cites MQA/GQA only for the structural reason the KV-head count is smaller than the query-head count; it does not claim a specific quality or speed result.

claims.claim: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct provides a representative GQA structure with 32 layers, 8 KV heads and head dimension 128; BF16 yields 128 KiB of K/V payload per token.
claims.notes: 1 GiB per 8192 tokens and 32 GiB for 32 requests are arithmetic examples, not measured allocations.

claims.claim: Current CacheConfig documents extensible KV cache sizing from memory remaining after warmup and CUDA graph capture, conditional gpu_memory_utilization defaults, and an explicit kv_cache_memory_bytes override.
claims.notes: Platform support and fallback behavior depend on device virtual-memory support.

claims.claim: Current CacheConfig exposes group-aware kv_cache_size_tokens and kv_cache_max_concurrency because num_gpu_blocks multiplied by one block size can be wrong for hybrid models with multiple KV groups.
claims.notes: Inspect startup logs and actual groups for hybrid, sliding-window, MLA and recurrent-state models.

claims.claim: vLLM supports FP8 KV Cache with scale and calibration paths; selected layer types can be excluded from quantization when supported.
claims.locator: FP8 KV Cache Overview, Scale Calibration, Skip Layers
claims.notes: Kernel/backend support is version-specific; fewer payload bytes do not guarantee identical quality or faster end-to-end latency.

claims.claim: V1 exposes Prometheus metrics including kv_cache_usage_perc, prefix_cache_queries, prefix_cache_hits, request_prefill_time_seconds, TTFT and inter-token latency.
claims.notes: Counters should be compared over consistent windows; queueing and workload shape affect latency.

claims.claim: The current KV Offloading Usage Guide describes OffloadingConnector support for CUDA, ROCm and XPU and CPU / secondary storage tiers.
claims.notes: Connector, tier and parallelism constraints apply; data movement latency can offset reuse gains.

claims.claim: The vLLM metrics endpoint exposes num_preemptions_total as a cumulative counter for preemption events.
claims.locator: Expected metric names in metrics endpoint tests
claims.notes: Compare counter increases over a time window rather than treating the cumulative value as a current rate.
